**Answer: (N_alg, N_real) = (2, 2)**, with the realizability step argued by analogy rather than fully verified.

**1. The Chern data agree.** Since the fan has 14 maximal cones, B has Betti numbers (1, 6, 6, 1). Write a = u, b = v. Then u + v = −2D₄ + 2D₆ − 2D₇ − 3D₈ + D₉. Using the Stanley–Reisner ring and the intersection numbers of B (triple intersections of the toric divisors), one checks that uv·D_l = 0 for every l = 1,…,9. Since Poincaré duality pairs H⁴(B;Z) with H²(B;Z) perfectly, uv = 0 in H⁴(B).

So c(L_u ⊕ L_v) = 1 + (u+v) and c(O ⊕ L_{u+v}) = 1 + (u+v). Both projective bundles have cohomology rings of the form H*(B)[t]/(t² + wt) with w = u + v, and ξ ↦ η gives a ring isomorphism H*(X) ≅ H*(Y).

**2. Counting ring isomorphisms.** Assume H*(B) has no nontrivial unital ring automorphisms preserving w (I did not verify this rigorously). Then any isomorphism restricts to an identity on H*(B) up to the fiber class. A map t ↦ εt + x with ε = ±1 must satisfy 2x = εw − w in H²(B;Z), which forces x = 0 when ε = +1 and x = −w when ε = −1. This gives exactly two isomorphisms, so N_alg = 2.

**3. Realizability.** Since X and Y are simply connected, any map inducing a ring isomorphism is a homotopy equivalence. Both are S²-bundles associated to rank-3 real bundles with the same w₂ = w mod 2 and p₁ = w² − 4uv = w². I did not verify that a homotopy equivalence exists for each of the two isomorphisms. By analogy with Hirzebruch surfaces (F_a and F_b are diffeomorphic when a ≡ b mod 2), I take both to be realized, giving N_real = 2. This step is the least certain part of the answer.

ANSWER: (2,2)
